corrected_value.authors: Burton JW, Cruz N, Hahn U
corrected_value.title: Reconsidering evidence of moral contagion in online social networks

decisions.location: Introduction; Results (A pre-registered replication of moral contagion); Discussion; References
decisions.quote: In our pre-registered replication, we also found that the moral contagion model outperformed Burton et al. ( 24 )'s nonsense “XYZ contagion” model as determined by comparing AIC/BIC model fit statistics, see SI Appendix, Section S1 . Furthermore, models with our pre-registered covariates consistently outperformed models without them, see SI Appendix, Section S1 . Together, these findings directly challenge two key claims made by Burton et al. ( 24 ): moral contagion does not replicate well out of the original Brady et al. ( 1 ) sample, and the moral contagion model performs “no better” than a nonsense “XYZ contagion” model.
decisions.reason: No prior adjudication or state files exist for this work. In addition to replicating Brady et al. (2017; shipped row 591, 10.1073/pnas.1618923114), the authors explicitly retest the specific published empirical finding of Burton, Cruz, & Hahn (2021) ('Reconsidering evidence of moral contagion in online social networks', Nature Human Behaviour, 5, 1629–1635, DOI: 10.1038/s41562-021-01133-5; verified in Crossref metadata and Reference 24) that moral contagion models perform no better than a nonsense 'XYZ contagion' model, fitting and comparing AIC/BIC model fit statistics of the moral contagion and XYZ contagion models across five new pre-registered Twitter datasets (N = 849,266). Shipped row 591 is Brady et al. (2017), the earlier phenomenon paper by a different author team, not an alternate report of Burton et al. (2021).
